knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: Publication Front chain
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. A portfolio records the number of claims made by each policyholder during one year. Which model placement is most defensible?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the correct classification and candidate family.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The recorded variable is a count regardless of the continuous observation period.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Treat annual claim number as discrete count data and assess an appropriate count distribution.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Classifying a variable by its time window rather than its possible values.

choices.label: This is a non-negative integer count, so a discrete count model such as Poisson is a candidate, subject to assumption checks.
It is continuous because a year is continuous, so Normal is mandatory.
It is categorical because some policyholders have zero claims.
It must be exponential because claims occur over time.

knowledge_checks.title: Revision Checkpoint: association honesty in the opening arc
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. A scatter plot shows a curved increasing association between advertising spend and policy sales. Which statement is most defensible?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The plot supports a descriptive association claim, not causal attribution.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Report the positive nonlinear association and avoid a causal conclusion.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Turning exploratory association into causation or assuming curvature means no association.

choices.label: The variables appear positively associated, possibly nonlinearly, but the plot alone does not show that advertising caused the increase.
The curve proves additional advertising causes additional sales.
Pearson correlation must equal zero because the pattern is curved.
A scatter plot cannot provide evidence about association between continuous variables.
